facts.value: Installs or restarts a supplied animation ID on a valid Fighter_GObj. ID -1 skips installation. Otherwise it invokes resource loading/resolution, records the ID, configures dynamics before assigning selected animation flags, installs the command-script pointer and clears loop_count. With x590 non-null it assigns flags and initializes playback at frame 0, rate 1, using the first blend byte as duration. It then clears the script timer and invokes ftAnim_8006EBA4 even when x590 is null. There is no direct motion-state transition call, but downstream script/callback state effects are not excluded.
facts.rationale: Replaces the baseline's absolute state-preservation statement with exact local behavior and conditional installation scopes.

evidence.why: Complete ordering, sentinel and resource guards.
Final processing includes action-script and other downstream calls.

facts.value: Source argument fp is Fighter*. It must identify a live Fighter; the predicate reads item_gobj and, when present, the item's hold-kind attribute without modifying these objects. Physical register assignment is not independently verified.
facts.rationale: Records the parameter's verified source-level role without asserting compiled ABI evidence.

evidence.why: Exact signature and guarded item access.

facts.value: Source argument gobj is Fighter_GObj*, providing the mutable Fighter and animation object. Fighter resolution precedes the anim_id sentinel guard; -1 is not a null-object safety guarantee. Physical register assignment is unverified.
facts.rationale: Documents argument role and sentinel ordering without overclaiming ABI or ownership.

evidence.why: Signature, resolution order and object use.

facts.value: Source argument anim_id is s32. -1 skips installation; other values directly index fp->x24 and fp->x28 without local bounds validation. This is an animation index, not a command to enter the motion state suggested by an enum token's spelling. Physical register assignment is unverified.
facts.rationale: Captures canonical type, boundary and semantic domain.

evidence.why: Sentinel, indexing and current animation assignment.

facts.value: Source argument gobj is Fighter_GObj*. It supplies the live Fighter for completion, held-item, kind and current-animation checks and subsequent installation. The owned body does not take ownership or register it for deferred work. Physical register assignment is unverified.
facts.rationale: Documents synchronous local use without asserting global callback safety.

facts.value: Source argument arg1 is an optional borrowed WaitStruct*. Null invokes current-animation installation. A used non-null table is read synchronously without mutation or retention: u.i.x == -1 terminates, u.i.y contributes cumulative weight, and the selected value is returned as (enum_t)u.p.x. Storage validity, appropriate union representation and valid selected indices are preconditions; compiled layout and physical register assignment are unverified.
facts.rationale: Preserves the exact union accesses rather than promoting the librarian's logical integer-pair shorthand to a representation guarantee.

evidence.why: Actual traversal, cast and null branch.

facts.value: Cycling is completion-gated. Null table or an item held by a fighter other than Fox/Mewtwo invokes current-ID installation; otherwise weighted draws are retried while equal to the current ID, except current IDs 2 and 31 allow repetition. No retry cap exists, so a table selecting only a disallowed current ID can loop forever. Thresholds are 1..100; weights are not normalized or validated, insufficient coverage can assert, and signed accumulation overflow has no defined recovery. Installation skips only -1, directly indexes metadata, calls dynamics before assigning selected flags, and resets/processes the script even with x590 null. Numeric repeat exceptions have no established visual mapping.
facts.rationale: Adds verified boundary, liveness and ordering details while keeping unsupported gameplay interpretation explicit.

evidence.why: All guards, selection, retries and installation ordering.
